- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# tidy-issues worker

The **acting** third of the repo tidy-up: triage the issues in scope, then record what you did. The run's
**Context section is binding scope** — it lists the issues to triage. Work only those; don't enumerate the
repo yourself. GitHub access is **MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`).

This task writes **issues only** (its triage actions and its own tracker). It never opens, closes, merges,
or comments on a PR, never touches a branch, and never pushes — those dimensions belong to `tidy-prs` and
`tidy-branches`, which are assess-only.

## 1. Triage each issue

For each issue in the Context list, run the [single-issue-triage](../../skills/single-issue-triage/SKILL.md)
skill. The skill owns the action ladder and the safeguards: "implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual
ask is true of `main`'s content **now** — verified there and cited, never inferred — and when the check is
inconclusive it **comments, doesn't close** — and an issue whose verdict is the one the skill
already posted there returns `unchanged`, written to nowhere. Collect what each triage did.

## 2. Reconcile this task's tracker

**Only a run that changed something reaches the tracker.** What counts is a triage action actually taken —
an issue closed, a comment posted — or something this run leaves for a human. `left` and
`unchanged` are not actions. A run that worked its whole Context list and took no action has
**nothing to record**: leave the tracker exactly as found, no body rewrite and no comment, and
create none if it doesn't exist. The scan itself is not news.

One standing tracker issue per repo, titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues` — found by that
**exact title, never a fuzzy match**; create it **already closed** when there is something to record and it
is absent — creation always lands an issue open and ignores a `state: closed` argument, so create it and
close it in a second call (never a fresh issue per run, never a bare number that can dangle). Each dimension
keeps its **own** tracker, so three tasks never race to rewrite one body.

Touch it two ways on a run that has something to record:

- **Rewrite the issue body** to today's **dated** snapshot: the actions taken this run and anything left
  for a human. The body is the live picture — it replaces yesterday's, it doesn't accumulate.
- **Add a dated comment** with today's status, so the body's snapshots leave a per-run trail.

Keep both short. **Never open, close, or reopen the tracker** — its state carries no meaning (the body is
the live picture; the state is just however it was created).

## 3. Retire the legacy tracker (transitional, one line of work)

Repos tidied before the split carry a single combined tracker titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Repo
Tidy`. If it exists and its body doesn't already say so, rewrite the body to one line pointing at the three
per-dimension trackers (`Tidy Issues`, `Tidy PRs`, `Tidy Branches`) and stop there — nothing else to do on
it, and never open, close, or reopen it. Already pointing at them ⇒ skip. Absent ⇒ skip; never create it.

`model: sonnet` — the implemented-in-`main` call is judgment; the reconcile is mechanical aggregation.

10	export default {
11	  id: 'tidy-issues',
12	  frequency: 'daily',                       // the 04:00 anchor (DESIGN §2) — the one tidy dimension that ACTS, so latency matters
13	  precondition_signals: ['issues', 'commits'],
14	  agent_model: 'sonnet',                    // "implemented in main" is a judgment call against main's current content
15	  expected_outcome: 'none',                 // writes ISSUES only (the triage actions + its own tracker) — never a PR
16	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
17	  agent_execution_timeout: 900,             // one dimension over a bounded issue list
18	
19	  // ONE trigger, and one widener. The trigger is a touched issue: if no issue was
20	  // filed, commented on, labelled, or reopened in the window, this task does not
21	  // run — the existing pile got the same triage last time it moved, and re-deriving
22	  // it costs an agent run per day to rewrite the tracker with itself.
23	  //
24	  // The task's own triage comments are the one write that lands on the issues this
25	  // gate watches, so re-announcing a standing verdict would arm tomorrow's run
26	  // forever (#988). single-issue-triage does not make that write; nothing here
27	  // filters it out after the fact.
28	  //
29	  // A substantive default-branch move WIDENS an already-triggered run to every open
30	  // issue, because a real commit can implement an issue the issue itself never
31	  // recorded — but it no longer wakes the task by itself. On any repo whose `main`
32	  // moves most days that widening was firing daily, which is a full re-triage of
33	  // every open issue every day: exactly the "went over the existing ones with
34	  // nothing new" this gate exists to prevent. A housekeeping-only move (a nightly
35	  // baseline commit, a bot bump) implements nothing, so it does not widen at all.
36	  precondition(signals) {
37	    const substantive = signals.commits?.substantiveChange === true;
38	    const open = (signals.issues?.open ?? []).map((i) => i.number);
39	    const touched = signals.issues?.touched ?? [];
40	
41	    // The issues signal already hides Claudinite's own issues — the queue's work
42	    // items and the standing trackers — so none can ever be triaged as project
43	    // work, nor count as the touch that triggers a run.
44	    if (!touched.length) return { run: false, reason: 'no issues touched in the window' };
45	
46	    const scope = substantive ? open : touched;
47	    return {
48	      run: true,
49	      reason: substantive
50	        ? `issues touched, and main moved substantively — re-check all ${scope.length} open issue(s) against it`
51	        : 'issues touched in the window',
52	      context: [`Issues to triage: ${scope.map((n) => `#${n}`).join(', ')}.`],
53	    };

1	# Claudinite work-item executor (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6, §10) — a pull worker
2	# over the queue. ONE RUN DRAINS THE QUEUE (§15.30, reversing §15.22's one-item
3	# run): Actions bills each job's minutes rounded up, so a run per item paid a
4	# whole invocation — checkout, setup, rounding — for each one. A run now settles
5	# its items one at a time until nothing is pickable, and the continuation job
6	# below covers a run that dies mid-drain. It carries NO cron of its own — the
7	# scheduler run's hourly dispatch, made when that run leaves something pickable,
8	# is the guaranteed delivery, so a lost `task:ready` label event is latency lost
9	# and never work lost.
10	#
11	# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE SECRETS LIVE (DESIGN §14). The wiring converge stamps
12	# every task's declared `required_secrets`, plus each configured invocation
13	# endpoint's token secret, into the step env below by name — the scheduler run and the
14	# janitor get none, because they never execute task code. Code-work is the only task
15	# code that ever sees a value; the agent hop carries nothing.
16	#
17	# MORE CAPACITY IS MORE EXECUTORS. Nothing enumerates them and each claim is
18	# independently leased, so a second job, a matrix width, or a runner outside
19	# Actions entirely all work — the executor's whole interface is issue read/write
20	# plus the repo at HEAD.
21	name: Claudinite executor
22	
23	on:
24	  issues:
25	    types: [labeled]
26	  workflow_dispatch:
27	    inputs:
28	      continuation_depth:
29	        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
30	        required: false
31	        type: string
32	
33	permissions:
34	  contents: write
35	  issues: write
36	  pull-requests: write
37	  actions: write
38	
39	jobs:
40	  execute:
41	    # A label event on anything else is not this workflow's business — and a
42	    # workflow_dispatch carries no label at all, so it always runs.
43	    # BOTH READY SPELLINGS, for as long as any fielded engine writes the legacy one
44	    # (#1119). A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing
45	    # here decodes — so this list is the one place the migration's two vocabularies
46	    # must both appear, and dropping the legacy spelling early makes every item an
47	    # older engine readies wait for the hourly scheduler run instead of starting now.
48	    if: >-
49	      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
50	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
51	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
52	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
53	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
54	    # The old cap — ≤ the engine's executing leash — retired with the heartbeat
55	    # (§15.15). A run is bounded by a DRAIN's work now, and a holder that is alive
56	    # says so on its item every 15 minutes, so the leash reclaims silence rather
57	    # than length. What is left here is a backstop against a wedged runner, well
58	    # clear of any declared `code_work_timeout`; a drain the platform kills at it
59	    # hands its remainder to the continuation job like any other dead run.
60	    timeout-minutes: 350
61	    steps:
62	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
63	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
64	        with:
65	          node-version: 24
66	      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
67	        env:
68	          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
69	          # The operator hold (DESIGN §8): set this repo variable to `true` and
70	          # every entry point exits at its first act, having fired nothing.
71	          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
72	          # The wiring converge stamps every declared required_secret, and every
73	          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
74	          # claudinite:secrets
75	          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
76	        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs
77	
78	  # A run that dies — crash, timeout, cancellation, runner loss — never reaches
79	  # its own re-dispatch, so without this the queue would sit until the next cron
80	  # fire. The platform runs this job on a FRESH runner after any such death
81	  # (DESIGN §10, S36), and its one step fires that dispatch instead: the
82	  # remainder drains in ~a minute, while the dead run's OWN item waits for the
83	  # executing leash to reclaim it — nothing here touches that item.
84	  #
85	  # `continuation_depth` is the stop. A run that dies at startup — a broken
86	  # engine, a revoked token — dies identically every time, and an unguarded
87	  # continuation would dispatch itself for as long as that lasts. After three the
88	  # chain stops and SAYS SO on the repo's workflow-failure issue: a queue that has
89	  # quietly stopped draining is the one failure nothing else here would surface,
90	  # since every individual run looks like an ordinary death.
91	  continue-the-chain:
92	    needs: execute
93	    if: failure() || cancelled()
94	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

# Claudinite work-item executor (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6, §10) — a pull worker
# over the queue. ONE RUN DRAINS THE QUEUE (§15.30, reversing §15.22's one-item
# run): Actions bills each job's minutes rounded up, so a run per item paid a
# whole invocation — checkout, setup, rounding — for each one. A run now settles
# its items one at a time until nothing is pickable, and the continuation job
# below covers a run that dies mid-drain. It carries NO cron of its own — the
# scheduler run's hourly dispatch, made when that run leaves something pickable,
# is the guaranteed delivery, so a lost `task:ready` label event is latency lost
# and never work lost.
#
# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE SECRETS LIVE (DESIGN §14). The wiring converge stamps
# every task's declared `required_secrets`, plus each configured invocation
# endpoint's token secret, into the step env below by name — the scheduler run and the
# janitor get none, because they never execute task code. Code-work is the only task
# code that ever sees a value; the agent hop carries nothing.
#
# MORE CAPACITY IS MORE EXECUTORS. Nothing enumerates them and each claim is
# independently leased, so a second job, a matrix width, or a runner outside
# Actions entirely all work — the executor's whole interface is issue read/write
# plus the repo at HEAD.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      continuation_depth:
        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A label event on anything else is not this workflow's business — and a
    # workflow_dispatch carries no label at all, so it always runs.
    # BOTH READY SPELLINGS, for as long as any fielded engine writes the legacy one
    # (#1119). A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing
    # here decodes — so this list is the one place the migration's two vocabularies
    # must both appear, and dropping the legacy spelling early makes every item an
    # older engine readies wait for the hourly scheduler run instead of starting now.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The old cap — ≤ the engine's executing leash — retired with the heartbeat
    # (§15.15). A run is bounded by a DRAIN's work now, and a holder that is alive
    # says so on its item every 15 minutes, so the leash reclaims silence rather
    # than length. What is left here is a backstop against a wedged runner, well
    # clear of any declared `code_work_timeout`; a drain the platform kills at it
    # hands its remainder to the continuation job like any other dead run.
    timeout-minutes: 350
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # The operator hold (DESIGN §8): set this repo variable to `true` and
          # every entry point exits at its first act, having fired nothing.
          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
          # The wiring converge stamps every declared required_secret, and every
          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
          # claudinite:secrets
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs

  # A run that dies — crash, timeout, cancellation, runner loss — never reaches
  # its own re-dispatch, so without this the queue would sit until the next cron
  # fire. The platform runs this job on a FRESH runner after any such death
  # (DESIGN §10, S36), and its one step fires that dispatch instead: the
  # remainder drains in ~a minute, while the dead run's OWN item waits for the
  # executing leash to reclaim it — nothing here touches that item.
  #
  # `continuation_depth` is the stop. A run that dies at startup — a broken
  # engine, a revoked token — dies identically every time, and an unguarded
  # continuation would dispatch itself for as long as that lasts. After three the
  # chain stops and SAYS SO on the repo's workflow-failure issue: a queue that has
  # quietly stopped draining is the one failure nothing else here would surface,
  # since every individual run looks like an ordinary death.
  continue-the-chain:
    needs: execute
    if: failure() || cancelled()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const depth = Number('${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}' || 0) + 1;
            const ref = context.payload.repository?.default_branch
              ?? context.ref.replace('refs/heads/', '');
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            if (depth <= 3) {
              await github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                workflow_id: 'claudinite-executor.yml',
                ref,
                inputs: { continuation_depth: String(depth) },
              });
              core.info(`the executor run died — dispatched a fresh one on ${ref} (continuation ${depth} of 3)`);
              return;
            }
            // The chain has died three times running: this is not one bad runner,
            // and dispatching a fourth would spend the day proving it. Escalate to
            // the same one-open-issue surface the scheduler's own failures use, and
            // let the hourly scheduler run be what tries again.
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite executor chain failed repeatedly';
            // The platform reporting its own failure IS an origin (`task:origin:github`),
            // and a chain that has died three times is a break to diagnose — the
            // `failure` park, the one lane that holds a task's lane (#1119).
            const labels = ['workflow-failure', 'task:origin:github', 'task:status:needs-human-failure'];
            const ensure = [
              { name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' },
              { name: 'task:origin:github', color: 'd4c5f9', description: 'Claudinite queue: filed by the platform itself — a workflow reporting its own failure' },
              { name: 'task:status:needs-human-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite queue: parked — the run broke, diagnose and fix' },
            ];
            for (const l of ensure) await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, ...l }).catch(() => {});
            const body = `Three consecutive executor runs died before finishing their item. The chain stops here; the next hourly scheduler run will dispatch a fresh one.\n\nThe last run: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels, body });
            core.setFailed('the executor chain died three times in a row — escalated');
